Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Porunnannore, PHC/CHC Vellamunda, Taluk Porunnannore, District Wayanad. Cases presented with fever, headache and fluid filled blisters. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Kanad ward 1 and ward 2 sub-district Agar, District Agar Malwa. Cases presented with symptoms Diarrhea, Vomiting. Four stool and two water Samples were sent to DPHL Microbiology lab Charak Bhawan Ujjain. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. 1 stool sample showed growth of salmonella on culture and water samples were found unfit for potable purpose. Cause of outbreak might be, mixing of drainage water with safe water supply through broken pipeline. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Matapur SHC Lokhandiya, sub-district Khaknar, District Burhanpur. Cases presented with symptoms Diarrhea, Vomiting. Three stool and two water Samples were sent to DPHL Indore. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All the lab results came normal. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Gardha, sub- district Saikheda, District: Narsinghpur. Cases presented with symptoms of loose stools, vomiting and pain abdomen. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from UPHC Paniwes, sub- district Jalna, District Jalna. Cases presented with fever nausea, vomiting and pain abdomen. 13 serum samples were sent to medical college lab of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Ten samples found positive for NS1 Ag for Dengue by ELISA. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Two deaths 22 yrs. old female and 2 months old baby succumbed to death. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene, sanitation and vector control measures.

Cases reported from Village Guhir, sub-district Vada, District Palghar. Cases presented with fever and body ache. 12 serum samples were sent to Model Rural Health Research Unit Lab. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Five samples found positive for IgM Dengue by ELISA. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene, sanitation and vector control measures.

Cases reported from Village Koloshi, sub- district Kankavli, District Sindhudurg. Cases presented with loose stools and pain abdomen. 5 water samples were sent to DPHL Sindhudurg. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All 5 samples found fit for potable purpose. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene, sanitation and vector control measures.

Cases reported from Village Kurai, sub-district Wani, District Yavatmal. Cases presented with loose stools, pain abdomen and weakness. 5 water samples were collected. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Two out of 5 samples found unfit for potable purpose. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene, sanitation and vector control measures.

Cases reported from Village Singjamei, sub- district Lamphelpat, District Imphal West. Cases presented with fever. Sixty-five samples were sent to VRDL-RIMS. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Twenty-Five samples out of sixty-five came positive for IgM Dengue by ELISA. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene, sanitation

Cases reported from Village Moolam ylliang, sub-district Saipung, District East Jaintia Hills. Cases presented with nausea, vomiting and blurred vision. District RRT investigated the outbreak. There is a history of consumption of mushroom, after that cases developed the symptoms. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene, sanitation

status: Case reported from Village Pyndengeri under
action: Nongstoin UPHC, Block Nongstoin District West Khasi Hills. Case presented with fever, aggressiveness, hydrophobia and aerophobia. District RRT investigated the outbreak. There was history of dog bite. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on awareness about human rabies and vaccination of cases and close contacts. 51 year old male succumbed to death on 03-07-2023.

Cases reported from Village Palasagora, sub- district Manamunda, District Boudh. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting. 3 water samples were collected. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Students of KGBV School developed the symptoms after taking tiffin and sweets during an exposure visit to a rice mill. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Gatirout patana sub-district Kandarpur, District Cuttack. Cases presented with loose motion. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were students of Ashram school. They developed the symptoms after consuming food from canteen. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Pillanallur, sub- district Rasipuram, District Namakkal. Cases presented with abdominal pain and nausea. One water sample collected and sent to DPHL Lab Namakkal. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were students of Sengunthar Mahajana Higher Secondary School residing in Adhi Dravida Welfare hostel. Water sample showed growth of Coliform bacteria. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Edaiyar palayam, sub-district Tiruchengode, District Namakkal. Cases presented with fever. Fourteen blood samples collected and sent to DPHL Lab Namakkal. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Result of samples came negative for Dengue NS1. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene, sanitation and vector control measures.

Cases reported from Village Uraie, sub-district Khaga, District Fatehpur. Cases presented with loose motion and abdominal pain. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Chlorine tablets distributed to the households. Chlorination of wells done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Savy Ville De Society, UPHC Rajnagar, District Ghaziabad. Cases presented with loose motion, vomiting and abdominal pain. Eight water samples were collected. District RRT investigated the outbreak. There was leakage in sewage treatment plant (STP) and water supply pipeline. Out of 8 water samples collected, 1 sample tested positive for E.coli. All cases treated symptomatically at a health camp organized in the society campus. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Jabarauli, sub- district Mohanlalganj, District Lucknow. Cases presented with fever with rash. Five blood samples were collected and sent to Virology lab KGMU, Lucknow. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Result came positive for Chickenpox (IgM ELISA). House to house survey done. Cases treated symptomatically. Cases were in the age group 15-30 years. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Kiriteswari, Binodpur, Taluk Nabagram district Murshidabad. Cases presented with abdominal pain, vomiting and loose stools. Three rectal swabs were sent to DPHL, lab MSD MCH. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All the cases have history of consumption of food at village fair. Stool culture came positive for E.Coli. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Kulidiyar Kamar Para, Taluk Farakka, District Murshidabad. Cases presented with abdominal pain, vomiting and loose stools. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All the cases have history of consumption of food at a marriage ceremony. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from sub-district Jaipur, District Purulia. Cases presented with Pain abdomen, vomiting, loose stool. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All the cases had consumed food at a function. House to house survey done. Cases treated symptomatically with ORS and iv fluids. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Nimdih, sub-district Nimdih, District Saraikela Kharsawan. Cases presented with loose stools. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. All the affected persons developed the symptoms after eating sweet. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on food hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Burzahama, sub-district Srinagar (North), District Srinagar. Cases presented with fever with rash. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Affected age group were 3 years to 28 years. House to house survey was conducted. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on importance of hygiene and sanitation.

Case reported from Village Kadappuram, PHC/CHC Kadappuram, Taluk Kadappuram, District Thrissur. Case presented with abdominal pain and vomiting. Serum and CSF samples collected and sent to NIV Alapuzha. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Both the samples came positive for IgM West Nile Virus by ELISA. 60-Year-old female succumbed to death on 04-07-2023 at 2:50 PM. Health educations was given. House to house survey was conducted and treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Gangaprasad, Taluk Berhampore, District Murshidabad. Cases presented with cutaneous lesion and fever. Two skin smears were sent to DPHL, lab MSD MCH. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Sample came positive for Bacillus anthracis on Gram’s staining. House to house survey was conducted. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases reported from Mandal Buchireddypalem, Village Pallaprolu. Cases presented with symptoms of Loose Stools (Watery). 4 Water samples were collected, out of which 2 were sent to RWS, Nellore and 2 were sent to IPM, Guntur. Nil Bacteriological Contaminants were found in Water. 4 stool samples were sent to Dept. of Microbiology, ACSR Medical College, Nellore. Stool samples were found to be positive for klebsiella in Stool Culture. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was conducted, medical camp was organized, alternate safe water supply was provided, chlorination of Water was done, and Cleaning/Repair of Clogged/Damaged water pipes was done. Health Education with support of Local Leaders/Influencers was given. Supply of ORS and Chlorine Tablets and Soaps to all households of affected hamlet was done. The outbreak might be caused by consumption of contaminated and stored food at a Death Ceremony on 12.07.23 (Afternoon).

Caseswere reported from Manjushree Vidyapith Residential School, Village Famla under Tawang block. Cases presented with itchy, fluid filled blister like rashes along with fever. Cases were clinically identified as chickenpox by treating physicians. The affected age group was in between 4-15 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Contact tracing has been done and accordingly isolated the active cases. Treatment was provided to all the active cases. IEC on prevention of chickenpox and personal hygiene was communicated to all the students and staffs of the school.

Cases were reported from Nagadum TE of Thaligram area under Udarbond Block. Cases presented with symptoms of Diarrhea and Dysentery. The affected age group was in between 7-18 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. Community was suggested to use boiled water to drink.

Cases were reported from Jonai CHC, Village Gali Mechaki, Sub-District Jonai. Case presented with symptoms of disturbed vision, nausea, labored breathing. Whole blood clotting time was tested in Jonai CHC which was found to be within 13 minutes, i.e. clotting time more than 12 minutes. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on snake bite. Awareness meeting and mike announcements were done in the district. An 80 year old male had expired due to Snake bite on 16-07-2023 at 3:40 AM.

Cases reported from Khagari Maijan Village, Dhupabor Maijan SC under Lahowal BPHC. Cases presented with fever with rash. 3 blood samples were sent to the Regional Medical Research Centre (ICMR) & WHO, Dibrugarh branch for measles/rubella testing. One blood sample showed Varicella Zoster Virus (VZV) and two blood samples were found to be negative on ELISA test by Regional Medical Research Centre (ICMR), Dibrugarh. On laboratory test of Measles Rubella by WHO at referral laboratory, Guwahati Medical College, one sample was found to be Measles positive and other two samples were found to be negative by ELISA test. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. IEC was done among people in that area. Medical team distributed acyclovir, vitamins, medicines and ORS to the affected children. Active search of cases was also done.

Cases were reported from Village: Behiating T.E., Sub-District: Dibrugarh West, District: Dibrugarh. Cases presented with symptoms of fever, abdominal cramp, loose stool with passage of mucus. Two drinking water samples from the loose water pipe and five stool swab samples sent to Microbiology Dept., Assam Medical College and Hospital, Dibrugarh for bacteriological examination. Result of one rectal swab samples shows growth of Shigella flexneri and other four samples shows no growth of enteric bacterial pathogen. The result of one water sample showed class 3 suspicious for drinking purpose and one water sample showed class 4 unsatisfactory for drinking purpose. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. The team gave awareness on hand washing, safe drinking water, use of latrine was given among the villagers and family members.

Cases reported from Rampur BPHC, Sub- District: Palasbari, District: Kamrup. Cases presented with symptoms of loose watery stool, fever, pain abdomen, vomiting. 10 rectal swabs and 4 water samples and Prashad (collected by FSO) were taken whose results were normal gut flora in case of rectal swab and Coliform bacteria was found in water samples. Samples were sent to DPHL, Kamrup to perform MPN test on water samples and culture on rectal samples and GMCH, Guwahati and Public Health Testing laboratory, Baminumaidam, Guwahati for testing. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. Medical team provided necessary medication. Mass health campaigning and awareness was given. The outbreak might be caused by consumption of black gram and whole green moong as "Prashad" on a religious ceremony held at an Ashram on 13.07.2023.

Cases reported from Village: Baro Gaon (Bara Gog), Sub-District: North Guwahati (Pt), District: Kamrup. Case presenyed with symptoms of hydrophobia, aerophobia, fever, weakness aggressiveness, fatigue, breathlessness, loss of appetite. The case a 45 year old female died on 14.07.2023 at around 7.20-7.30 pm due to rabies. ARV was given to the close contact of the deceased and family members. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on rabies. Further verbal autopsy was done regarding the case and further case finding was conducted in and around that area for the next few weeks.

Cases were reported from Village: Baruajani, Sub-District: Kamalpur, District: Kamrup. Cases presented with mild fever, body pain, and headache. 15 blood samples were collected and sent for testing at DPHL, Kamrup, out of which 12 were found to be Leptospirosis positive by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on VBD. Awareness was given along with mass health camps and regular monitoring of any similar cases was done.

Cases reported from Health facility: Balajan, District: Kokrajhar. Cases presented with symptoms of Fever, headache and vomiting. 9 cases were found positive for malaria (one was found to be mixed and 8 were pf) on Peripheral blood smear and by RD kit. Blood samples were sent to Balajan BPHC which were all found to be positive for malarial parasite. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on VBD. ITBN, LLIN were distributed. Mass BS collection, fogging and testing and fever surveillance was done.

Cases reported from Village: Rohdhala, Matiparbat, Hatibat Simaluguri & Amalapatty, District: Marigaon. Cases presented with symptoms of fever with headache. 5 CSF & Serum samples were sent to DPHL Morigaon, GNRC Dispur Guwahati which were found to be JE IgM ELISA positive. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Fogging was done. Bed nets were impregnated in the affected area. Health education was given. IEC, BCC was done. Leaflet distribution was done.

Cases were reported from Dhing UHC, North Haiborgaon, Buragohainthan PHC, Hatipara village, Bhakatgaon village and Digholdori, Barapujia BPHC. Cases presented with symptoms of Fever, seizure, unconsciousness and Vomiting. 4 CSF samples were sent to DPHL, Nagaon, the result was, 2 were Negative, 1 was Equivocal and 1 was found to be positive for JE IgM ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Fogging was done. Bed nets were impregnated in the affected area. Health education was given. IEC, BCC was done. Leaflet distribution was done. One case a 55 years old Female expired on 27-07- 2023 at GMCH, Guwahati.

Cases were reported from Station Chariali, Urban Ward Sivasagar, Nemuguri Bokota and Bokota, Na Nathgaon under Demow BPHC, Dupdor Chariali and Chengdhoragaon under Geleky BPHC. Cases presented with Fever, altered sensorium and unconsciousness. 6 CSF samples were sent to Microbiology Dept., AMCH, all were found to be positive for JE IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Fogging was done. Bed nets were impregnated in the affected area. Health education was given. IEC, BCC was done. Leaflet distribution was done.

Cases were reported from Village: Hardas Bigha, Sub-District: Khusrupur, District: Patna. Cases presented with loose stools, nausea and vomiting. 1 stool sample and water sample were collected. Stool culture came negative for any entero-pathogen. Cause of outbreak might be due to broken pipeline, which was repaired later. A 4 year old child succumbed to death due to the illness. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village: Boriavi, Sub- District: Anand Rural, District: Anand. Cases presented with symptoms of abdominal pain, vomiting &decrease appetite. 6 water& 6 serum samples were sent to DPHL, Petlad &Civil Hospital, Petlad, all serum samples tested for hepatitis were non-reactive (by rapid test) & all water samples tested had E.coli in them & were not satisfactory for drinking. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases reported from PHC Bisru, CHC Punhana. Cases presented with symptoms of generalized maculopapular vesicular rash with Concomitant presence of papules, blisters, pustules. The affected cases were in the age group of 5-15 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on fever with rashes. Group meeting with ASHAs, AWWs, ANM, School teachers of Govt. School and Community leaders of the village.

Cases reported from Digiana Wno. 45 Slum falls under UPHC Digiana. Cases presented with itchy skin rashes all over the body. All the cases belong to the age group of 9 to 14 years in which 2 were Males and 4 were Females. Mother and Child Protection (MCP) cards were not available and Children were partially vaccinated for routine vaccines as per verbal communication with parents. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. Vaccination of Left out and dropout children was done.

Cases reported from Government Upper Primary school, Village Adijan Adwan, Block Shopian, District Shopian. Cases reported with pain, tenderness and swelling in one or both parotid glands. All the 13 cases were isolated till their recovery. The affected age group is in between 04-16 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team to the inhabitants regarding mumps. IEC were distributed.

Cases were reported from Village: Garapathar, HSC Tarni, Sub-District: Jamtara, District: Jamtara. Cases presented with Fever with Rash. 6 serum samples have been sent to RIMS Ranchi, which came positive for IgM Varicella zoster virus (VZV). Symptomatic treatment had been given to prevent from chicken-pox. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village: Jariya, Sub-District: Torpa, District: Khunti. Cases presented with Fever with Rash. 5 serum samples have been sent to RIMS Ranchi, All came negative for measles and chickenpox. Symptomatic treatment had been given to prevent from chicken-pox. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village: Bhargaon, Sub-District: Lohardaga, District: Lohardaga. Cases presented with Fever with Rash. 5 serum samples have been sent to RIMS Ranchi, out of which four samples came positive for IgM VZV (Varicella zoster virus). The affected age group was in between 6-12 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Chandrapur Village under CHC Panki. Cases presented with symptoms of fever with rash. 6 serum samples were sent to DPHL Palamu, all were found to be positive for IgM VZV (Varicella zoster virus). The affected age group was in between 8-11 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village: Barannad, Sub- District: Jagannathpur, District: West Singhbhum. Cases presented with Fever with Rash. 5 serum samples have been collected, out of which two samples came positive for IgM VZV. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases reported from Morarji Desai Residential School, Yadavanhalli village, PHC Horeyala limits, Gundlupet Taluk, Chamarajanagra District. Cases presented with symptoms of Pain abdomen and vomiting. The affected age group is in between 12 to 16 Years. 4 water samples were tested at PHC Horehala, in which all samples were SPP (suitable for potable purpose).District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. The outbreak might be caused by consumption of Chicken curry on 16.07.2023 for dinner.

Cases reported from Hounshi Village, PHC Havanur limits, Haveri Taluk, Haveri District. Cases presented with symptoms of loose stools and vomiting. 2 water& 1 stool samples were sent to DPHL Haveri. Both the water samples were found to be SPP (suitable for potable purpose) & stools sample was found to be negative for Vibrio and entero-pathogens .District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Case reported from VillageRudnoor &Kamarwadi Thanda, Rudnoor PHC limits& CHC Wadi limits, Chincholi Taluk& Chittapur taluk respectively, Kalaburagi District. Cases presented with fever of more than 7 days.2 Blood samples collected at PHC Rudnoor & CHC Wadi were sent to DPHL Kalaburagi, both were found to be positive for Leptospira by IgM ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases reported from Y N Hosakote Village, PHC Lingadahalli Limits Pavagada Taluk, Tumkur District. Cases presented with symptoms of Loose stools and vomiting.3 stool &14 water samples were sent to DPHL Tumakur. The stool samples did not yield any pathogens and 6 water samples were NSPP (not suitable for potable purpose) &8 were SPP (suitable for potable purpose). District RRT investigated the outbreak. Isolation of cases was done. House to house survey was done. Community awareness on drinking ORS water, boiled water, stop drinking bore well source water & consume potable water.

Cases reported from Kanvihalli village, Nandi Bevur PHC limits, Harapanahalli Taluk, Vijayanagar district. Cases presented with symptoms of loose stools and vomiting. 5 stool samples and 21 water samples were sent to VIMS Ballari and Nandi Bevur PHC Lab respectively. 2 stool samples were found to be positive for Vibrio by hanging drop. Out of 21 water samples 4 were NSPP (not suitable for potable purpose). The most affected age group was in between 21-60 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community was advised to immediately stop suspected contaminated water source and to use alternate water supply. 24x7 temporary clinics were setup with sufficient HR (human resource) and drugs, IV fluids and also ambulance facility 24x7. Isolation of cases was done. Daily House to house survey was done. Community awareness regarding hand washing practices, food hygiene and advised to drink boiled cool water and to consume fresh and hot food.

Cases reported from Village Kottapuram, PHC-CHC Alangad, Taluk Varappuzha, District Ernakulam. Cases presented with symptoms of fever, headache, abdominal pain, loose stools and vomiting. The most affected age group is 30 to 45 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. The outbreak might be caused by consumption of common source of food by all the affected cases.

Cases reported from Village Ukawad Khurd, Sub-District Bamori, PHC Fatehgarh. Cases presented with symptoms of loose watery stools. 5 rectal swab samples were sent to the GRMC medical college Gwalior. Vibrio Cholera serotype isolated after 48 hours from the samples. The affected age group was in between 15-60 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Door to door survey by health team was done. Community awareness especially regarding seasonal disease prevention, advice to use boiled water for drinking purposes and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases reported from Village Mohpani,SC Tendukheda, Block Salichouka, Sub-District Gadarwara, District Narsinghpur. Cases presented with symptoms of Cold with fever, headache, body pain and weakness. 36 samples were sent to CHC Kareli, District Narsinghpur for RDT-Kit test and Blood Slide examination. Out of the 36 samples tested by RDT- Kit 8 were found to be Positive for malaria & all Blood slides were found to be negative for malarial parasite. The most affected age group was in between 21-30 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Fever survey, Larval Survey & Entomological survey were done. Health camp was organized in the village & treatment was given to the affected cases. Spraying/fogging in the village was done. IEC regarding using of mosquito net was given. PRI (Panchayati Raj Institution) members, villagers, health workers meeting was conducted.

Cases reported from Saraiha, CHC Mauganj, Sub-District Mauganj, District Rewa. Cases presented with symptoms of abdominal pain, vomiting, shivering. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to House survey was done. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. The outbreak might be caused by consumption of food in a gathering by all the affected cases.

Cases reported from District DH (district hospital) Ujjain, PHC Panthpiplai. Cases presented with symptoms of Diarrhea and vomiting.3 Water Samples were collected and sent to DPHL Ujjain which were tested using K019 H2S Medium (Powder). The water of all the 3 samples was found to be contaminated with Salmonella or Citrobacter. The affected age group was in between 15-20 Years. All cases were from a training camp which is organized at Prashanti institute of engineering. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. A team of medical doctors was stationed at the event site.

Cases reported from Village Narsiyapalli, Block Sironcha, PHC- Moyabinpetha, SC Narsiyapalli. Cases presented with Fever of more than 7 days, Headache, fatigue. 15 Samples were sent to DH Gadchiroli and IGMC, Nagpur, out of which 10 were found to be Positive for Dengue by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Fever mass survey was conducted. Health education was given. Containers were examined& positive containers were emptied. Aggressive IEC Regarding malaria & dengue prevention was given. Fogging & spraying was done.

Cases reported from Village Padoli, Jagji and Warwanti, SC Takwiki, PHC Patoda, Block Osmanabad. Cases presented with symptoms of Fever, weakness. 7 serum samples were sent to GMC Solapur, out of which 4 were found to be positive for Dengue by IgM ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Fever survey was done. IEC Regarding dengue prevention was given. Fogging & spraying was done.

Cases reported from Umberade UPHC, Kalyan Dombivali Corporation Area. Cases presented with symptoms of Fever, weakness. 2 samples were sent to Civil Hospital Thane for Malaria and Dengue testing both samples were found to be negative. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Fever survey was done. Dengue handbills were distributed in the affected area. IEC Regarding dengue prevention was given. Fogging & spraying was done. Water tanks& Fridge were checked for larvae. Temephos & oil were mixed in water tanks.

Cases reported from HUD Coimbatore, Block Coimbatore Corporation West Zone, PHC 49 Goundampalayam, HSC Housing Unit, Village Ambethkar Nagar. Cases presented with fever. The affected age group is in between 5-10 years. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. Tab. acyclovir was given to the affected cases. Fever camp was conducted in school. Isolation of cases was done.

Cases reported from HUD Salem, Block Sankari, PHC Thevur, HSC Pullagoundampatti, Village Keelur. Cases reported from District Jail Alappuzha, Village Allissery, PHC W&C Alappuzha, Taluk Ambalapuzha. Cases presented with symptoms of fever with rash. All cases were diagnosed clinically. Cases reported from Village Puthenpalam, PHC Thalayazhom, Taluk Edayazhom. Cases presented with diarrhea and vomiting. All the cases attended a function at the index case’s house on 07-09-2023. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on hygiene, and sanitation. The outbreak might be caused by consumption of contaminated food by all the cases.

Cases were reported from HWC Umari, Village Bheron Ghhati, Block Bhadora Guna. Cases presented with symptoms of fever with rash, cough and cold. All the cases were diagnosed clinically. Health education imparted regarding the spread of disease. Contact tracing & fever survey was done. Health camps were organized.

Cases were reported from Village Rajgarh Ward no. 15, Block Sirmour. Cases presented with symptoms of diarrhea and vomiting. The affected age group was 5 to 55 years. Five stool samples were collected and sent to DPHL DH Rewa and 2 water samples were sent to PHE Rewa. All samples were found to be normal. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on drinking of boiled cool water and hand washing practices and food hygiene and given awareness regarding importance of safe & pure drinking water. Establishment of temporary clinic in the affected village was done. Daily house to house survey was conducted along with ORS distribution. Death of a 25 year old female has occurred due to the illness.

Cases were reported from CHC Badagaon, Village Amarpur, Sub-District Tikamgarh. Cases presented with symptoms of loose watery stool with weakness. Four stool samples were sent to BMC, Sagar, in which no microbial growth was found on culture. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team about drinking of boiled cool water and hand washing practices and food hygiene, and given awareness regarding importance of safe & pure drinking water. Establishment of temporary clinic in the affected village was done. Daily house to house survey was conducted along with ORS distribution. Three deaths have occurred due to the illness of an 80 years old male, 27 years and 60 years old females.

Cases reported from Kalyan Nagar,UPHC Sanjivani Nagar, Amaravati Municipal Corporation. Cases presented with symptoms of fever & weakness. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral health team on dengue. Fever and container survey were conducted in the surrounding areas, and preventive and curative measures were taken. Daily entomological surveys were conducted. Fogging, source reduction was done. A 22 year old male died due to sudden cardiac respiratory arrest, convulsions, dengue hemorrhagic shock, and appendicitis with thrombocytopenia with acute febrile illness.

Cases reported from At./Po. Saidapur, PHC Madalmohi, Block Georai. Cases presented with symptoms of fever, body ache, headache & weakness. A 2 year old male child died due to dengue.

Cases of Hepatitis A were reported from PHC Thalappalam, Village Thalappalam, Sub-District Meenachil, District Kottayam. Cases presented with fever, loss of appetite, nausea. Six blood samples were sent for testing, out of which two were positive for Hepatitis A IgM by ELISA. LFT results of five serum samples showed elevated bilirubin, SGPT and SGOT levels, consistent with hepatic inflammation. Environmental surveillance revealed a pit latrine located 8 meters from a contaminated public well, which tested positive for E.coli and coliform bacteria. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community health education was provided on sanitation and safe water practices.

Cases were reported from FHC Manimala, Village Manimala, Sub-District Kanjirappally, District Kottayam. Cases presented with fever, vomiting and nausea after consumption of contaminated food or water in a social gathering on 1st and 14th May 2025. All age groups were affected. Total 73 samples were collected & sent for testing, out of which 54 were positive for HAV IgM by card test, 2 by CMIA, 4 by ELFA, and 13 by ELISA. Water samples from the venue tested positive for E.coli. District RRT investigated the outbreak, and awareness was raised about safe water and hygiene practices.

Cases were reported from PHC Kizhakkoth, Village Kizhakkoth, Sub-District Thamarassery, District Kozhikode. Cases presented with fever, fatigue, anorexia and vomiting, mainly among residents using water from a common water supply. Six samples were sent to RPHL & MCH, all were positive for Anti-HAV IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were conducted on safe water usage and hygiene.

Cases were reported from PHC Kunduthode, FHC Maruthomkara, Village Kavilumpara, Sub-District Vatakara, District Kozhikode. Cases presented with fever, fatigue, anorexia and vomiting, after attending a wedding event on 12th May 2025. Two samples were sent to Malabar Institute of Medical Sciences (MIMS) Kozhikode, both were positive for Anti- HAV IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was provided on hygiene, sanitation, and safe drinking water practices.

Cases were reported from FHC Vanimel, Village Vanimel, Sub-District Vatakara, District Kozhikode. Cases presented with fever, fatigue, anorexia, and vomiting, linked to a death anniversary function held on 4th May 2025, attended by around 100 people. One sample was sent to MIMS KKD, which was positive for HAV IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were conducted on hygiene and safe water use.

Cases were reported from CHC Vallana, Villages Kidangannur and Aranmula, Sub- District Kozhenchery, District Pathanamthitta. Cases presented with fever. Ten blood samples were tested at St. Thomas Hospital Malakkara, CHC Vallana, Muthoot Hospital, CM Hospital, DH Kozhencherry, out of which eight were positive for Dengue by rapid test and two for NS1 by ELISA. District RRT conducted field investigations. Fogging and source reduction were carried out. Community awareness activities were conducted focusing on vector control.

status: Cases were reported from a School under
action: CHC Erumapetty, Village Kariyannur & Nelluwaya, District Thrissur. Cases presented with vomiting and loose stools after consumption of food from a common place. Eleven students were hospitalized in Al Ameen, Amala Hospital and MCH Thrissur. Three water samples were tested at Kerala Water Authority's Quality Control Sub-District Laboratory in Kizhakkumpattukara, Thrissur, in which Coliforms and E.coli were detected. District RRT investigated the outbreak, and health education was provided. Preventive measures, including disinfection of classrooms and food hygiene awareness sessions, were undertaken.

Cases were reported from FHC Vettilappara, Village Athirappally, Sub- District Chalakkudy, District Thrissur. Cases presented with fever. Total 20 blood samples were sent for testing, out of which eighteen were positive for Dengue by rapid test and one for NS1 by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Breeding sources such as tarpaulin sheets and water containers were found. Source reduction, fogging, and public awareness activities were undertaken.

Cases were reported from GH Kalpetta, Village Kalpetta, Sub-District Vythiri, District Wayanad. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education on hygiene, sanitation, and preventive measures were carried out by the peripheral health team.

Cases were reported from Village Chhirvel, PHC Barud, Block Chhegaon Makhan, District East Nimar. Cases presented with diarrhea. All age groups were affected. Eight rectal swabs and three water samples were collected and tested at DPHL Indore. Rectal swabs showed normal flora & water samples tested positive for fecal coliform bacteria. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and water safety. House-to-house surveillance was conducted. Suspected wells were immediately disconnected, and chlorination was carried out daily.

Cases were reported from Villages Padariya and Bhaluha, Sub-District Huzur, District Rewa. Cases of diarrhea were reported after attending a marriage event. One stool and one water sample were tested at DPHL DH Rewa, all were negative for Cholera or any pathogen. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on food safety and sanitation. House-to-house surveys & health camps were conducted. Four deaths have occurred due to the illness, including a 1- year-old male, two elderly individuals aged 80 and 81, and a 17-year-old female.

Cases were reported from Village SansarPur, Sub-District Mangawan, District Rewa. Cases presented with symptoms of loose watery stools. The affected age group was15-44 years. Two stool and one water sample tested negative for Cholera & any pathogen at DPHL DH Rewa. Four patients were referred to the Medical College, two were admitted at CHC Gangeo, and others received home-based treatment. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene and sanitation. Surveillance was done.

Cases were reported from Village Bothiya, Sub-District Keolari, District Seoni. Cases presented with diarrhea and vomiting. Water samples were tested by the PHE department. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and safe water practices. House- to-house surveys and chlorination of water sources was done. The outbreak might be caused by consumption of contaminated bore well water.

Cases were reported from Village Jalgaon Arvi, PHC Talegaon Dashasar, Sub-District Dhamangaon Railway, District Amravati. Cases presented with fever with chills, fatigue, headache, and malaise. The most affected age group was 15-44 years. A total of 44 blood samples were collected and tested at DMO Lab Amravati, out of which 27 were positive for Malaria (Plasmodium vivax) by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Control measures included source reduction, dry day observation, guppy fish introduction, Temephos application, and fogging. Community awareness and health education were given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Duseguda, Block Etapalli, SC Punnur, PHC Kasansur, District Gadchiroli. Cases presented with high-grade fever and altered sensorium. One blood sample was collected and tested at District Hospital Gadchiroli. Out of 154 tested, 3 were positive for Malaria (Plasmodium falciparum) by rapid test. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House-to-house fever surveillance, container survey, and health education were carried out by the peripheral team focusing on vector control, hygiene, and sanitation. One death was reported: a 25-year-old female, who died on 09/06/2025 at Civil Hospital Gadchiroli (positive for Malaria).

Cases were reported from Jivba Nana Jadhav Park area, Sub-District Karvir, District Kolhapur. Cases presented with fever and malaise. All age groups were affected. Total 40 blood serum samples were collected and tested at SSH, out of which 6 were positive for Dengue IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene, and sanitation. House-to-house fever surveillance was conducted. Source reduction, removal of breeding sites, destruction of stagnant water, fogging for three consecutive days, and solid waste clearance were carried out. Personal protection measures and environmental vector control were promoted. Death of a 25 year old male has occurred due to the illness on 10.06.2025.

Cases were reported from Ward 6, Bhivapur Urban, Sub-District Bhiwapur, District Nagpur. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting, linked to a wedding ceremony on 12-06-2025. The most affected age groups were 15-25 and 40-60 years. Seven stool samples were collected and tested at RPHL Nagpur; all were negative for Cholera. Seven food samples, four water samples, and six stool samples were collected and sent to RPHL Nagpur and GMC Nagpur for further investigation. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases were admitted to RH Bhivapur. Community awareness and health education were provided by the peripheral team on food safety, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Kachari Savanga and Bhorgad, Sub-District Katol, District Nagpur. Cases presented with loose motion, vomiting, fever, and abdominal pain. All age groups were affected. Three stool and three water samples were collected and tested at RPHL Nagpur and GMC Nagpur; all were negative for any entero-pathogen. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Super chlorination of drinking water was conducted. Community awareness and health education were provided by the peripheral team on safe drinking water practices, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Sonari, Sub-District Uran, District Raigad. Cases presented with fever, body ache, and weakness. The most affected age group was 21–30 years. Four blood samples were tested at the Sentinel Center, Thane, out of which one was positive for Dengue NS1 Antigen by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Fogging and spraying activities were conducted. Daily fever surveillance, source reduction (abating), and community awareness through IEC activities were undertaken by the peripheral health team on vector control, hygiene, and sanitation. Death of a 25-year- old male have occurred on 12/06/2025 at Panacea Hospital, Uran.

Cases were reported from Village Kuapali, Sub-District Paikamal, District Bargarh. Cases presented with symptoms of vomiting, nausea, and loose motion, linked to food consumed during a religious gathering attended by approximately 700 people. Seven rectal swab and three water samples were tested at IPHL Bargarh. All rectal swabs were negative for any entero- pathogens. Water samples were negative for H2S test & OT value of 0.0 PPM. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were given on hygiene and sanitation. House-to-house survey and treatment were given, including ORS distribution. Water disinfection and community sensitization activities were undertaken.

Cases were reported from Sub-District Bhadrak Rural, District Bhadrak. Cases presented with fever with rash. The affected age group was 1-5 years, predominantly male. Five serum samples were sent to ICMR-RMRC, Bhubaneswar, all tested negative for measles. Among the cases, 89% were previously vaccinated. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on control measures and sanitation. IEC activities were carried out, and Vitamin A was administered. Hygiene, nutrition, and isolation were emphasized.

Cases were reported from Village Suanri, Sub-District Tangi, District Cuttack. Cases presented with vomiting and loose motion. Four rectal Swabs and water samples were sent to SCB MCH. All rectal swabs were positive for Vibrio cholera. Water samples were positive for H2S test & OT value of 0.0 PPM. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene and sanitation. Mass disinfection, contact dose administration, and perimeter surveillance were conducted. District and state teams responded with house-to-house surveys. ORS and medicines were distributed. Death of a 75-year-old female had occur due to the illness.

Cases were reported from Villages Gholapur and Tulasipur, Sub-District Banki, District Cuttack. Cases presented with symptoms of loose motion and vomiting. Three rectal swabs and water samples were collected and tested at SCB MCH. All water samples tested positive for H2S with an OT value of 0.0 PPM. One rectal swab tested positive for Vibrio cholerae. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and disease prevention. Administration of contact doses, mass disinfection in affected villages, perimeter surveillance, house-to-house surveys, and distribution of ORS and necessary medicines was done. Water disinfection was done.

Cases were reported from Village Jhinkiria, Sub-District Cuttack Sadar, District Cuttack. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting after consuming food during a marriage feast. Two rectal swabs and two water samples were collected for laboratory testing. All water samples tested negative for H2S with an OT value of 0.0 PPM, and no entero-pathogenic organisms were detected in rectal swabs. District RRT investigated the outbreak. IEC/BCC activities on safe food and drinking practices, house-to-house surveys was done. ORS and other necessary medications were provided, and water disinfection was carried

Cases were reported from Danagadi CHC, Village Tarailo, Sub-District Tomka, District Jajapur. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting after consumption of food from a common place. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Dharmasala CHC, Village Pakhara, Anjira & Godipatia, Sub-District Dharmasala, District Jajapur. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting after attending a social gathering on 08.06.2025. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Bato, Sub-District Sainkul, District Kendujhar. Cases presented with symptoms of loose motion and vomiting. Three rectal swabs and three water samples were collected and sent to SCB MCH, Cuttack. All water samples tested positive for H2S with an OT value of 0.0 PPM. No entero-pathogenic organisms were detected in rectal swabs. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Administration of contact doses, mass disinfection of the affected village, perimeter surveillance was done. House-to- house surveys were conducted. ORS, zinc tablets, and Halazone tablets were distributed. A mobile medical team visited the village regularly, and community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and safe water practices. The suspected source of infection was contaminated water supply from the village overhead tank. Two deaths have occurred due to the illness (60 year/male and 42 year/female).

Cases were reported from Village Champapal, Sub-District Ghasipura, District Kendujhar. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting. One rectal swab and two water samples were collected and tested at SCB MCH, Cuttack. All water samples tested positive for H2S with OT value of 0.0 PPM. No entero-pathogenic organisms were found in rectal swab. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and water safety. Administration of contact doses, mass disinfection of affected areas, perimeter surveillance was done. ORS and other essential medicines were distributed. House-to-house surveys were conducted. The source of infection was suspected to be contaminated bore well. One fatality was reported of a 55-year-old female due to the illness.

Cases were reported from Villages Chakaliguda and Cherengaguda, Sub- District Koraput, District Koraput. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting. A total of 2 rectal swabs and 12 water samples were collected; all water samples tested negative for H2S with an OT value of 0.0 PPM and rectal swabs showed no entero-pathogenic organisms. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and safe drinking water practices. House-to-house active surveillance, health team deployment (24x7), contact dose administration, and disinfection of dug wells every alternate day was done. Community meetings were held to demonstrate Halazone tablet usage, hand washing, and ORS preparation. Daily & night surveillance was conducted. Water from dug wells was suspected as the source of infection.

Cases were reported from Villages Parichhipur and Khiripada, District Mayurbhanj. Cases presented with fever and jaundice, primarily affecting females in the 1-10 year age group. A total of 31 blood and 3 water samples were collected. Water samples tested negative for H2S with OT value of <0.01 PPM. Five blood samples tested positive for HAV IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and preventive measures. House-to-house surveys, water disinfection was done.

Cases were reported from Village Binishpur, Sub-District Rayagada, District Rayagada. Cases presented with fever and rash. Seven blood samples were collected and sent to DPHL Rayagada, of which 4 tested positive for Malaria (3 for Plasmodium vivax & 1 for Plasmodium falciparum) and 3 tested positive for Dengue NS1 Ag by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. IEC activities, house-to-house surveys, and education on maintaining proper hygiene, nutrition, and isolation was done.

Cases were reported from JRM UHP, Sub- District Coimbatore South, District Coimbatore. Cases presented with vomiting and diarrhea. Majority of the cases were more than 15 years of age. Three water samples were collected from different locations (OHT, middle tap and tail-end tap) & tested at Chief Water Analyst’s Laboratory, and one additional sample tested at DPHL Coimbatore. All four water samples tested negative for contamination. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and safe water practices.

Cases were reported from Village Thirumullaivasal, PHC Thirumullaivasal, Block Kollidam, District Mayiladuthurai. Cases presented with fever and blister-like skin rash. One blood sample was sent to Kings Institute, Guindy, Chennai, which tested negative. All cases were diagnosed clinically. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on personal hygiene, infection control, and isolation of cases to prevent further spread.

Cases were reported from an old age home in Pattakurichi, PHC Sundarapandiapuram, Block Tenkasi, District Tenkasi. Cases presented with symptoms of loose or watery stools and vomiting. All affected cases were more than 15 years of age. Total 4 stool, 2 food, and 6 water samples were collected & sent to DPHL Chokkampatti & Regional Water Lab, Tirunelveli. One food sample was positive for E.coli, and 5 water samples were positive for fecal coliforms on culture. Water samples showed presence of contamination with E.coli, fecal streptococci, Salmonella, Shigella, and Clostridium perfringens. Stool samples tested negative on culture. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and safe food and water consumption practices. Active case surveillance, water chlorination, food safety interventions were done and community education was given. Six deaths (40-74 years age group, including 3 males & 3 females) have occurred during the outbreak.

Cases were reported from a Hostel in Block Pattukottai, District Thanjavur. Cases presented with loose stools. The most affected age group was 15 years and above. Total 4 water, 3 stool, 1 blood, and 1 food sample were collected & tested at DPHL Kumbakonam and Food Safety Office. Two water samples were positive for contamination & all 3 stool samples were negative for any entero-pathogen. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided by the peripheral team on control measures, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Thirukkurungudi Town Panchayat (Wards 3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15), Thirukurungudi CHC, Block Kalakad, District Tirunelveli. Cases presented with symptoms of vomiting, loose stools, and lower abdominal pain. The most affected age group was 15 years and above. A total of 5 stool samples and 10 water samples were collected & sent to Regional Water Lab, Tirunelveli and Micro Lab TVMCH. Two water samples were positive for E.coli, Fecal Streptococci and Clostridium perfringens. Stool cultures were negative for any entero-pathogen. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided by the peripheral team on control measures, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Sirumadurai Colony, Block Iruvelpattu, District Villupuram. Cases presented with symptoms of diarrhea. The most affected age group was 15 years and above. One stool sample was collected and tested at GVMCH Villupuram, which was negative for bacterial pathogens by culture. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education on safe drinking water, sanitation, and personal hygiene was provided to the affected community.

Cases were reported from Village Kalvimadai, PHC A.Mukkulam, Block Narikudi, District Virudhunagar. Cases presented with loose stools after attending a religious gathering. Majority of cases were more than 15 years of age. Three stool and three water samples were collected & sent to DPHL Virudhunagar. All three stool samples tested negative for any entero- pathogen. Two water samples were found to be contaminated. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene, sanitation, and safe drinking water practices.

Cases were reported from Village Bagpali, Sub-District Bhanoli, District Almora. Cases presented with fever. Three blood samples were sent for testing, all were positive for Salmonella paratyphi A by TyphiDot/RDT. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Amlai (Meya Para), Sub-District Nalhati-I, District Birbhum. Cases presented with loose stools and abdominal discomfort. The most affected age group was 15-44 years. Two rectal swab samples were collected and sent to RGMCH for testing. The suspected cause of the outbreak was consumption of contaminated water. District and block RRT teams investigated the outbreak. House-to- house surveys were conducted. Medicines such as Halogen, ORS were distributed. Disinfection of the water source was carried out. Health workers conducted IEC activities and meetings with the local community to raise awareness on safe water use, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Keshabpur, Sub-District Arambagh, District Hooghly. Cases presented with symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal discomfort. The suspected source of the outbreak was consumption of street food from a local vendor. The most affected age group was 5-14 years. Five water samples and three rectal swab samples were collected and sent to the National Institute for Research in Bacterial Infections. Food Safety Officer collected food & water samples, which were sent to WBPHL laboratory for testing. District RRT investigated the outbreak. A medical camp was organized. Essential medicines and ORS were distributed. Health education and community awareness were provided regarding food safety & hygiene.

Cases were reported from Butaldinni Village, PHC Harapura, Taluka Sindhanur, District Raichur. Cases presented with symptoms of vomiting and loose stools. All age groups were affected. A total of 9 cases were hospitalized (2 in Taluka Hospital and 4 in private facilities). One stool sample was collected and tested at RIMS Lab. Hanging drop test was negative, and culture showed no growth after 48 hours. A total of 18 water samples were collected. Six water samples were tested at Harapura PHC using the H2S method, out of which 4 samples were found unfit for drinking. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

A case of West Nile Fever was reported from Village Ambalappuzha, Sub-District Ambalappuzha, District Alappuzha. The patient, a 63-year-old female, presented with fever, headache, and seizure. She had a history of intracranial surgery with chronic limb weakness. She was admitted to Government TD Medical College, Vandanam, treated in the ICU, and discharged on 29th May without neurological complications. Her blood sample tested positive for West Nile IgM at NIV Alappuzha. Fever survey, source reduction, larvicide spraying, and fogging were carried out. No additional suspected cases were found, and household contacts tested negative. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education activities on vector control, hygiene, and sanitation were conducted.

Cases of fever with jaundice were reported from Villages Thamarakkulam and Vallikunnam, Sub-District Mavelikkara, District Alappuzha after attending a wedding event on 1st and 3rd May 2025. Eleven samples were sent for testing, all were positive for Hepatitis IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene and sanitation. One death of a 48-year-old male due to Hepatitis A occurred on 14th June at AIMS Kochi (positive for Hepatitis A).

Cases were reported from Villages Pallikunnu and Azhikode South, Sub-District Kannur, District Kannur. The index case, a 32-year-old female, passed away on 15th April 2025. A total of 11 cases were reported from the surrounding areas after attending the funeral of the index case on 15.04.2025. The most affected age group was 4-17 years. Water samples from the household well were sent to Kerala Water Authority Quality Control Sub-District Laboratory, Kannur (Pallikunnu), which showed contamination with E.coli and coliform bacteria, indicating it as the probable source. Four samples were sent to ASTER MIMS & RPHL, all were positive for HAV IgM by ELISA. Follow-up water samples revealed increasing contamination levels. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education activities were carried out focusing on water safety, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from SDH Darwha, Sub-District Darwha, District Yavatmal. Cases presented with fever. Total 57 blood smears were collected and tested, out of which four were found positive for Malaria. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Fever mass survey and entomological surveillance were conducted. Community awareness and health education were given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene, and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Asanagir, Sub-District Nathavaram, District Anakapalli. Cases presented with vomiting and loose stools. District RRT investigated the outbreak. All the cases developed the symptoms after eating food in a hotel on 15- 06-2025 during their visit to a festival. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Twin City (Itanagar and Naharlagun) Sub-District Itanagar EAC, District Papum Pare. Cases presented with fever, chills, bodyache. 6 blood samples were collected and sent to DPHL-TRIHMS. They were tested positive for Scrub typhus IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. They were treated at the hospital. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Saruthe kerabari, Sub-District Mangaldoi (Pt), District Darrang. Cases presented with loose stools and vomiting. Rectal swab and 1 water sample were tested. Rectal swab did not show growth of any pathogenic organism. Water sample found fit for potable purpose. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. All the cases developed the symptoms after attending a birthday party. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Thangal gaon no. 3, under Joriguri Subcentre, Sub-District Moran, District Dibrugarh. Cases presented with loose stools, fever, headache and vomiting. 2 Rectal swabs and 1 water sample were collected and sent to AMCH, Dibrugarh. Rectal swab found positive for Salmonella. Water sample found unfit for potable. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. All the cases developed the symptoms after having food in a social gathering on 19-06- 2025. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Dholai Molai, Sub-District Katlichara, District Hailakandi. Cases presented with fever with rash. 27 blood samples were collected and sent to GMCH, Guwahati. All the samples found negative for measles. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Age group of the affected cases was 1-15 years. Cases treated symptomatically. All the cases were vaccinated. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Villages Buragaon & Molia Gaon, Sub-District Titabor, District Jorhat. Cases presented with fever with rash. 10 blood samples were collected and sent to JMCH. 7 samples found positive for the Varicella Zoster IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Taroud, Sub-District Balod, District Balod. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting. 4 stool samples and 21 water samples were collected and sent to Medical College Rajnandgaon. Stool samples did not show growth of any pathogenic organism. 5 water samples found unfit for potable purpose. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Tarrighat, Sub-District Patan, District Durg. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting. 7 stool samples and 4 water samples were collected and sent to Hamar lab Raipur and PHE Department respectively. 2 Stool samples came positive for Vibrio Cholerae. Water samples found unfit for potable purpose. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Lamkeni, Sub-District Abhanpur, District Raipur. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting. 2 stool samples were collected and sent to Hamar Lab, Raipur. Stool samples did not show growth of any pathogenic organism. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Balisana, Sub-District Patan, District Patan. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Asoj, Sub-District Vaghodia, District Vadodara. Cases presented with loose motion and vomiting. 1 stool sample and 4 water samples were collected and sent to SSG Vadodara Hospital. It was tested negative for Cholera on culture. All the water samples found unfit for potable purpose. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Sub-District Dhanbad-Cum-Kenduadih-Cum-Jagata, District Dhanbad. Cases presented with Jaundice. 6 blood samples were collected and sent to SNNMCH, Dhanbad. All samples tested positive for Hepatitis A IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Age group of the affected cases were 1-21 years. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Bhabhri, Sub-District Gumla, District Gumla. Cases presented with fever with rash. 12 blood samples were collected and sent to RIMS, Ranchi. 5 samples found positive for the Varicella Zoster IgM by ELISA District RRT investigated the outbreak. Age group of the affected cases were 6-26 years. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Villages Amidha, Kutmu and Luhur Sub-District Barwadih, District Latehar. Cases were found during routine fever surveillance after receiving the news of typhoid case in the village. 25 blood tested positive for Salmonella paratyphi A by RDT kits and Widal test. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Affected cases were from all age groups. Cases treated symptomatically. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from a Training School, Khanapur, Village Bacholi, Ashok Nagar & Amboli, Sub-District Khanapur, District Belagavi. Cases presented with symptoms of abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea, following consumption of street food and contaminated water. The affected age group was 35-40 years. Cases were admitted to General Hospital, Khanapur. Two stool sample and two water samples were collected & tested at BIMS Microbiology Department. Stool samples showed normal commensals on culture. One water sample was found unfit for consumption. District RRT investigated the outbreak. (Entomological indices: HI 8.19%, CI 41.17%, BI 22.95%)

Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene and infection prevention.

Three stool and two water samples were tested at DPHL Indore. Stool samples showed normal flora; water samples were found unsatisfactory. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Isolation and symptomatic management were done. Chlorine tablets distributed. Community educated on safe water and food practices.

Cases were reported from Village Galthani, Sub-District Pohri, District Shivpuri, presenting with cough, fever, conjunctivitis, and runny nose. The affected age group was 1-15 years. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases were reported from Village Majhgawan, SHC Kodar, PHC Dhamokhar, Sub-District Manpur, District Umaria. Cases presented with fever and rash. The affected age group was 1-20 years. Six blood samples were collected and sent to NIRTH Jabalpur, all were negative for Measles. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Administration of Vitamin A doses to all affected individuals, household fever and rash survey was done. Community awareness and health education on hygiene, sanitation, and control.

Cases were reported from Village Newali, Mahavan SC, Lateri Block, District Vidisha. Cases presented with vomiting and diarrhea. The affected age group was 20-40 years. Twelve water samples were collected and sent to PHE Department, with two samples found to be contaminated with fecal coliform and total coliform counts exceeding 2400. Three stool samples were sent to Microbiology Department, Government Medical College Vidisha, where one sample tested positive for Vibrio cholerae. District RRT investigated the outbreak. A 15-day health camp was organized. IEC activities on safe drinking water and hygiene, distributing ORS, zinc, and chlorine tablets to all affected households, and daily chlorination for 15 days was done. Tankers were arranged for safe drinking water supply. The outbreak was attributed to contamination of drinking water.

Cases were reported from Village Rudhadi Pr. Khatkali, Sub-District Akot, District Akola. Cases presented with symptoms of abdominal pain, loose motion, and nausea. All affected cases were above 15 years of age. One stool sample & two water samples were tested at DPHL Akola. Stool sample was negative for Cholera, while two water samples were found contaminated. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided by the peripheral team on hygiene, sanitation, and outbreak prevention. Daily house-to-house surveillance, chlorination of all water sources, and the use of Mediclor for water purification was done.

Cases were reported from Village Gilbili, Sub-District Ballarpur, District Chandrapur. Cases presented with fever and cough. A total of 9 samples were collected and sent to AIIMS Nagpur, out of which 1 was positive for Scrub Typhus by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak and carried out community awareness activities to control the spread and educate the public. Surveillance activities, including entomological survey and fever survey, were conducted in the affected area. Vector control measures such as Malathion dusting and extensive IEC campaigns on disease prevention, hygiene, and sanitation were conducted. One death, of a 56-year-old female, has occurred due to Scrub Typhus with complications of meningitis, sepsis, and multi-organ failure on 23/06/2025.

Cases were reported from Jahagirdarwadi Village under PHC Yedshi, Block Dharashiv. Affected individuals were majorly in the 5 to 15 years age group, presented with fever. A total of 11 blood smear samples were collected and sent to the DMO office for testing, out of which 3 tested positive for Malaria (one each for Plasmodium vivax & Plasmodium falciparum and a mixed infection of P.vivax and P.falciparum). District RRT investigated the outbreak. Two rounds of abetting, fogging operations were conducted in the affected area, and intensive health education and awareness campaigns focusing on hygiene, sanitation, and vector control was done.

Cases were reported from Village Rewadi, SC Devi, PHC Malpur, Taluka Shindkheda. Cases presented with fever, body ache, and chills. The affected age group ranged from 12 to 63 years. A total of 7 samples were tested at Late Shree Bhausaheb Hirey Government Medical College Lab, Dhule, out of which 3 were positive for Malaria (Plasmodium vivax) on peripheral smear microscopy. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation. Daily house-to-house surveys, container surveys, fogging, abating were done.

Cases were reported from Village Kharde, SC Untavad, PHC Kharde, Taluka Shirpur, District Dhule. Cases presented with symptoms of loose motion, abdominal pain, and nausea. The affected age group ranged from 5 years to 56 years. A total of 5 stool samples were collected and tested at Late Shree Bhausaheb Hirey Government Medical College, Dhule, out of which 2 were positive for Vibrio cholerae by microscopy (hanging drop preparation). District RRT investigated the outbreak. Daily house-to-house surveys, health education, scientific use of TCL powder for drinking water purification, village cleanliness drives, and testing of TCL and water samples was done.

Total 49 blood smears (BS) were tested by Rapid Diagnostic Kits at PHC Murumgaon, confirming 2 cases of Plasmodium falciparum & 1 case of Plasmodium vivax. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Health education was given on the importance of completing malaria treatment and the use of mosquito nets. Community awareness activities were conducted focusing on vector control measures, personal hygiene, and sanitation to prevent further transmission. One death was reported of a 55-year-old female, who died on 21/06/2025 at Civil Hospital Gadchiroli due to Malaria.

District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided on hygiene and sanitation practices. Daily field surveillance, water quality checks, chlorination of water sources, and distribution of Mediclor for disinfection was done.

Additionally, a water sample collected & sent to the Chief Chemist Water Testing Laboratory, PHED, Mizoram, was found to be satisfactory. District RRT investigated the outbreak. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education given by peripheral team on control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Fifteen water samples were collected and sent to Microbiology Lab at AGMC, which were found to be potable. Total 34 blood samples were collected and sent to AGMC, Tripura, out of which one tested positive for Hepatitis A (IgM by ELISA). All other cases were epidemiologically linked. All cases were treated symptomatically. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided regarding safe drinking water and sanitation practices.

District RRT investigated the outbreak. Community awareness and health education were provided regarding safe drinking water, hygiene, and sanitation. Pipeline leakages were repaired. A health camp was organized in the locality, where cases were treated. ORS packets and chlorine tablets were distributed. The suspected source was contamination of drinking water due to mixing of pipeline water with sewage.

District and Block RRT investigated the outbreak. Chlorination of the overhead tank was carried out and pipeline leakages were repaired. Community awareness and health education were provided regarding safe drinking water and proper sanitation. One death of a 59-year-old male has occurred due to severe dehydration and shock on 25.06.2025.

A CSF sample was collected and tested at Bongaigaon DPHL, which was positive for JE IgM by ELISA. District RRT investigated the outbreak.
